%%abcts what `letter_to_bar` reads past a barline for its ending label: whitespace, an
%%abcts optional `[` absorbed into the barline's own length, then a token of
%%abcts `1234567890-,` — and NOTHING when that token is empty or opens with a `-`,
%%abcts which reverts the `[` too (`abc_parse_music.js:868-887`).

fixture/abcts-rests-and-bars.header:
%%abcts shapes neither corpus writes, swept through both engines one at a time. Two of
%%abcts these are rules; four are open rows, measured through abcjs 6.7.0 and NOT built:
%%abcts   X:4  !trill!z4     BUILT. A rest takes its decorations like any element, after
%%abcts                      its own glyph — and X:9 is the MULTIMEASURE case, which is a
%%abcts                      SECOND call with its own box. One shared call, whose box has
%%abcts                      to be invented, took three of that ladder's rungs off exact.
%%abcts   X:5  {g}z2         BUILT, on two terms neither of which was guessable from the
%%abcts                      page width: the grace group's own WIDTH is left ink on a rest
%%abcts                      exactly as on a note, and the slur's far anchor is the rest's
%%abcts                      declared PITCH — its box's midpoint — not where its glyph is
%%abcts                      drawn. Printing a graced note's fields beside a graced rest
%%abcts                      (`left=10.00` against `left=0.00`) is what named the first.
%%abcts        ⚠️ AND abcjs ITSELF WRITES `M NaN` for the grace flag on `{g}x2` — a bug of
%%abcts        its own, and the one shape here that byte parity could reach only by
%%abcts        reproducing a NaN. See Docs/ABCJS-DIFFERENCES.md.
%%abcts   X:6  [K:G] mid-bar BUILT — it prints where it stands, on the same index the
%%abcts                      meter and the clef beside it already used.
%%abcts   X:7  [M:2/4] mid-bar BUILT — any NON-NOTE element ends the beam, and an inline
%%abcts                      field is one. Ours beamed all four notes as a run.
